COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) ADVISORY COMMITTEE

Welcome to the meeting of the Community Development Block Grant Advisory Committee. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling (818) 548-2090.
Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/departments/management-services/gtv6/watch-city-
meetings. PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE MSB 105.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon
request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign
language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206.
If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

  SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
  Friday, February 21, 2020, 9:00 a.m.
  Municipal Services Building, 633 E. Broadway, Room 105, Glendale, CA 91206

A SPECIAL MEETING of the CDBG Advisory Committee is hereby called to meet at 9:00 a.m. on Friday,
February 21, 2020, in the Municipal Services Building , 633 E. Broadway, Room 105, Glendale, CA 91206
to consider the following item of business, to wit:

1.  ROLL CALL
  A. Report of Recording Secretary re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the February 21, 2020
  special meeting of the CDBG Advisory Committee was posted on or before Thursday, February 20,
  2020, at 9:00 a.m., on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  INTRODUCTIONS and PRESENTATIONS
  A.  Recognition of Armineh Hoonanian for 15 years of service to the Community Development Block
  Grant program

3.  MINUTES
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the October 23, 2019, CDBG Advisory Committee Special Meeting

4.  BUSINESS AGENDA

  A.  Reports – Information Only
  1. Community Capital Improvement Project Status
  2. Second quarter FY 2019-20 social service performance reports and expenditure rates
  3. Financial Ratios for community organizations
  4. Review proposal evaluation process; and interview and deliberation protocol

  B.  Action Items
  1.  Capital Improvement Funding Recommendations for FY 2020-2021
  a.  Options for Allocating Remaining Capital Improvement Funding for FY 2020-21
  b.  Conduct interviews with capital improvement applicants; and deliberate and approve
  funding recommendations
  2.  Social Service Funding Recommendations for FY 2020-2021
  a.  Conduct interviews with social service applicants; and deliberate and approve funding
  recommendations
 5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes. The
  Commission may question the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. Staff may refer the
  matter to the proper section or department for investigation and report.

6.  COMMITTEE/STAFF COMMENTS

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  Onnig Bulanikian
  Director of Community Services & Parks

  -------
  ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SERVICE
  Members of the public may address the CDBG Advisory Committee regarding any item in this notice.
  Service of the above Call for Special Meeting of the CDBG Advisory Committee, at the time and place
  above designated, is hereby acknowledged, and the Notice required by Government Code Section
  54956 is hereby waived:
  Hour:  a.m./p.m., this  day of  , 20 .
  By: ____________________________Title: CDBG Advisory Committee Member
minutes_text:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) ADVISORY COMMITTEE

  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
  Friday, February 21, 2020, 9:00 a.m.
  Municipal Services Building, 633 E. Broadway, Room 105, Glendale, CA 91206

1.  ROLL CALL
  The meeting began at 9:05 a.m.

  Present: Gharibian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Armenian, Avedisian
  Absent: None
  Staff:  Bulanikian, Aleksanian, Kavarian, Moreno Hernandez

  A.  Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the agenda for the February 21, 2020 special meeting
  of the CDBG Advisory Committee was posted on or before Thursday, February 20, 2020, at
  9:00 a.m., on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  INTRODUCTIONS and PRESENTATIONS
  A. Recognition of Armineh Hoonanian for 15 years of service to the Community Development
  Block Grant program
  Ms. Hoonanian was not available to attend, and therefore, the item was tabled.

3.  MINUTES
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the October 23, 2019, CDBG Advisory Committee Special
  Meeting

  A motion was made to approve the October 23, 2019 minutes of the CDBG Advisory
  Committee special meeting as submitted.

  Moved: Ramirez  Second: Gharibian

  Approved by unanimous consent.

4.  BUSINESS AGENDA

  A.  Reports – Information Only
  1. Community Capital Improvement Project Status

  Senior Community Services Specialist Maggie Kavarian introduced Erik Adamyan, the
  new program specialist for the CDBG program, who then provided a status update on
  the FY 2019-20 Capital Improvement Projects.
  {{section.number}}{{item.number}}
   Chair Avedisian and Committee Member Gharibian asked if any agencies have asked
  for extensions to complete their projects. Ms. Kavarian replied that the projects are
  still in the environmental phase and that once the Environmental Impact Reports are
  completed, contracts will then be finalized with the agencies with completion dates set
  for one year from the contract execution date.

  Vice-Chair Armenian asked if, when managing capital improvement projects, staff
  questions the sequencing of projects where one project may affect another. He
  mentioned Homenetmen’s current proposal for its roofing project as an example,
  which would require removal of solar panels previously funded by CDBG. He said that
  he would bring up this question during item 4B1b.

  2.  Second quarter FY 2019-20 social service performance reports and expenditure rates

  Ms. Kavarian gave a PowerPoint presentation with an overview of the FY 2019-20
  Social Service projects, stating that most agencies are on track to meet their proposed
  outcomes and expend their awarded funds. She said that the exception is AGBU,
  which did not start its program until February 18, 2020, but staff has been in
  communications with them and are now confident that AGBU will be able to meet their
  goals and expend their funds.

  Vice-Chair Armenian asked if the reported numbers served is for clients that meet the
  CDBG criteria, to which Ms. Kavarian replied affirmatively, explaining the verification
  process. Vice-Chair Armenian expressed his concern that AGBU might not be able to
  expend the funds by the end of the fiscal year, and explored the option with staff to
  reallocate the funds to another agency.

  Committee Member Gharibian also expressed his concerns with what would happen if
  AGBU was not able to expend the funds.

  3.  Financial Ratios for community organizations

  Ms. Kavarian provided a PowerPoint presentation on the CDBG ratio calculation
  process.

  Vice-Chair Armenian and Committee Member Gharibian asked questions relating to
  how the analysis of Glendale/S. Glendale Boy Scouts of America Verdugo Hills
  Council is affected by the fact that Boy Scouts of America filed for bankruptcy recently.

  4.  Review proposal evaluation process; and interview and deliberation protocol

  Ms. Kavarian provided an overview of the schedule for the rest of the meeting.

B.  Action Items
  1.  Capital Improvement Funding Recommendations for FY 2020-2021
  a.  Options for Allocating Remaining Capital Improvement Funding for FY 2020-21

  Ms. Kavarian gave a PowerPoint presentation reporting that the final FY 2020
  entitlement allocation from HUD in the amount of $703,359 for City of Glendale
  Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) was greater than the amount previously
  {{section.number}}{{item.number}}
   estimated by staff and included in the approved FY 2020-21 RFP for CIP. She
  further reported that the YMCA of Glendale had submitted a proposal, but
  withdrew its funding request, leaving only two applicants requesting a combined
  total of $317,258. She explained the Committee’s options for allocating the
  remaining minimum of $386,101after making funding recommendations for the two
  applicants.

  Public Comment:
  Moises Carrillo, Catholic Charities of Los Angeles, Inc. – requested consideration
  for allocating funds to Catholic Charities for an emergency roofing project. Ms.
  Sandra Yanez also answered questions on behalf of the agency.

  After asking questions to Catholic Charities and staff, the Committee decided to
  table this item until after item 4B1b.

  The Committee began deliberations on this item after taking action on item 4B1b.

  After much discussion, a motion was made to utilize the remaining FY 2020-2021
  Community/Neighborhood Capital Improvement Project (CIP) funds in the amount
  of $386,101 to pay off the balance of the Section 108 Loan Repayment, including
  interest, in the amount of $241,135, and to allocate the remaining $144,966 to the
  Pelanconi Park Playground and Shade Structure Project.

  Moved: Gharibian  Second: Ramirez

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Gharibian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Armenian, Avedisian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

  Item 4B2 was taken next.

b.  Conduct interviews with capital improvement applicants; and deliberate and
  approve funding recommendations

  The following interviews were conducted:
  1. Main Campus Roofing Installation Project – Homenetmen Glendale “Ararat”
  Chapter
  2. Glendale Community Center Facility Improvements – Catholic Charities of
  Los Angeles, Inc.

  Regarding Catholic Charities of Los Angeles, Inc.’s request to receive funds for a
  roofing project for which they did not submit a proposal, the Committee agreed
  that it would not be fair to other agencies for them to approve it. However, they
  said they would consider approving them for funding for the project they applied
  for with a modified scope of work.

  Committee members had a lengthy discussion about how to handle requests to
  change the scope of a project from what was included in the proposal.

  {{section.number}}{{item.number}}
   After much deliberation, a motion was made to approve a funding
  recommendation in the amount of $123,988 for Catholic Charities of Los
  Angeles, Inc.’s FY 2020-21 Glendale Community Center Facility Improvements
  Project as amended to replace the kitchen cabinetry part of the scope with roof
  replacement.

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Ramirez

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Gharibian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Armenian, Avedisian,
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

  After some deliberation, a motion was made to approve a funding recommendation
  in the amount of $193,270 for Homentemen Glendale Ararat Chapter’s FY 2020-
  21 Main Campus Roofing Installation Project.

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Gharibian

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Gharibian, Ghazarian, Armenian, Avedisian,
  Noes:  Ramirez
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

  The Committee returned to item 4B1a. at this time.

2.  Social Service Funding Recommendations for FY 2020-2021
  a. Conduct interviews with social service applicants; and deliberate and approve
  funding recommendations

  The following interviews were conducted:
  1. Loaves and Fishes Program - Catholic Charities of Los Angeles, Inc.
  2. Homeless Outreach Case Management - Ascencia
  3. Intervention/Prevention Clinical Group Counseling - Committee for
  Armenian Students in Public Schools (CASPS)
  4. LA Troupe Fire/Burn Prevention Education for Elementary School Aged
  Children - Children’s Burn Foundation
  5. While Housing Rights Center was scheduled for an interview regarding
  its Fair Housing Program, they did not appear.
  6. The Zone - The Salvation Army
  7. Community Outreach Program - Armenian Relief Society of Western
  USA, Inc.
  8. Housing Support for Homeless Families – Family Promises of the
  Verdugos
  9. Youth Development Through Scouting – Glendale/S. Glendale Boy
  Scouts of America Verdugo Hills Council
  10. Intergenerational Experiences – Armenian Cultural Association,
  Hamazkayin

  {{section.number}}{{item.number}}
   11. After School Program/Teen Mentoring/Therapy Program – Door of
  Hope
  12. Scholarship Program – Academy USA
  13. Afterschool Youth Enrichment Program – Armenian Cultural Foundation
  14. Youth Employment Program – Glendale Youth Alliance

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Ghazarian

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Gharibian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Armenian, Avedisian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained:  None

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

6.  COMMITTEE/STAFF COMMENTS

  {{section.number}}{{item.number}}
   Committee members thanked fellow committee members, staff, and applying agencies.

  Committee Member Gharibian left the meeting at 5:17 p.m.

  Ms. Kavarian announced a community meeting taking place on March 26, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. at
  the Adult Recreation Center to receive input from the public on the 2020-2021 Annual Action
  Plan, as well as a City Council/Housing Authority meeting tentatively scheduled for April 14 at
  3:00 p.m. She also announced that the 2nd Annual Glendale Non-Profit Summit would be
  taking place the morning of March 6, 2020 at the Central Library.

7.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at: 5:25 p.m.
